entity.name: Ansel Co-Op
entity.description: Ansel Co-Op is the organisation behind Ansel, an open-source raw photo editor for artists, forked from darktable in 2022 by Aurélien Pierre and maintained since October 2025 by Jiyoné (Guillaume Stutin). Everything under github.com/aurelienpierreeng is funded here: the editor, its documentation in 10 languages, the developer documentation at dev.ansel.photos, the website in 9 languages, and the research code around them — VirtualSecretary, LensSerious, ansel-denoise. The websites are served by GitHub Pages from a static CMS, so they cost nothing to host; what the project actually pays for is the ansel.photos domain name (30 €/year) and the AI subscriptions used for development and documentation (90 €/month plus VAT each, for two developers — 216 €/month; Anthropic declined to sponsor the project). Money given to this team is split among the people doing the work, by public takes. The ultimate goal is a co-operative in which the users actually own the project; pending that legal structure, this Liberapay team keeps the boat afloat. Everything the project makes is free and stays free: no rewards, nothing to unlock. The founder's personal work — his websites, writings, music and the repositories on his own account — is funded separately at https://aurelienpierre.com/funding.json.

projects.name: Ansel
projects.description: An open-source raw photo editor for artists — a darktable fork (2022) that keeps the imaging science and trims the rest. 1,000+ stars, GPL-3.0, nightly builds for Linux, Windows and macOS. Carries the scene-referred pipeline its founder wrote (filmic RGB, tone equalizer, color balance RGB, diffuse or sharpen, guided-Laplacian highlight reconstruction) and, since 2026, the color equalizer module, scene-referred raster drawing and the Canvas layout-and-print atelier.

projects.name: Ansel documentation
projects.description: The user manual and the developer documentation of Ansel: about 55 module pages translated into 10 languages, published at ansel.photos/doc, plus the developer-facing documentation at dev.ansel.photos. Written and maintained alongside the software rather than after it.

projects.name: Virtual Secretary
projects.description: A Python framework building the missing knowledge layer over documentation, mailboxes, calendars and third-party sources. It powers Chantal, a semantic search engine over 47,000 pages of photography and raw-processing documentation that answers about 1,100 questions a month, free and without an account, and an email/agenda automation engine that files and tags mail from rules written against real context.

projects.name: LensSerious
projects.description: Lens-correction mathematics as data rather than as a runtime. Lensfun's community database is excellent but its runtime fights a modern raw pipeline: 8.4 MB of XML parsed into flat lists at every startup (89–102 ms measured), linear fuzzy scans, and a process-global setlocale() flipped during parsing. LensSerious keeps the database and drops the runtime: CPU/SIMD/OpenCL-ready closed forms, parity-tested against liblensfun.

projects.name: ansel-denoise
projects.description: Training pipeline for Ansel's neural raw denoiser, working in the CFA domain with synthetic supervision derived from measured camera noise profiles — denoising before demosaicing, where the noise actually is.
